ux.l1.why.messageNew: {bot} asked because {name} is someone new. Once this goes, {name} counts as known.
ux.l1.why.messageNewAsk: {bot} asked because {name} is someone new. Once this goes, {name} counts as known. At Ask, every send asks.
ux.l1.why.messageSeveral: {bot} asked because {n} of these people are new.
ux.l1.why.messagePublic: {bot} asked because this posts in public on {where}.
ux.l1.why.deleteOutside: {bot} asked because this deletes outside its own folder.
ux.l1.why.pay: {bot} asked because paying asks at Ask, Auto and Full access.
ux.l1.why.payRoutine: Paying asks on every routine run.
ux.l1.why.askOwner: {bot} asked because it is on Ask: you approve each action.
ux.l1.why.askRoutine: {bot} asked because this run of {routine} is at Ask.
ux.l1.why.webhook: {bot} asked because this started from a webhook, so it does each step with you.
ux.l1.why.channel: {bot} asked because this came in from {channel}. Your own messages there skip approvals only when you turn that on under Full access.
ux.l1.why.channelUnnamed: {bot} asked because this came in from a channel message. Your own messages there skip approvals only when you turn that on under Full access.
ux.l1.why.unattended: {bot} asked because nobody started this from your computer or your phone, so it does each step with you.
ux.l1.why.alwaysAsk: This could wipe this computer, so Murage asks every time, at every level.
ux.l1.why.sensitiveGuard: This reads a key or password file, so Murage asks at every level.
ux.l1.why.unreadCall: Murage could not read this whole, so it asks. Allow it once if it is right.
ux.l1.why.destructiveGuard: This looks destructive, so Auto asks. Full access runs it without asking.
ux.l1.why.promptGuard: This command may wait for a password or input nobody would see, so Murage asks.
ux.l1.why.stopGrantNote: Murage will not ask about {place} again. It still asks when a command could wait for input or reads a key.
ux.l1.why.recipientNotNoted: Murage could not note {name} as known, so the next email to {name} asks again.
ux.l1.fold.heading: {verb}, and stop asking
ux.l1.fold.footer: {bot} stays on {level}. Take any of these back under {bot} › Level.
ux.l1.fold.footerPhone: {bot} stays on {level}. Take back this conversation's and routine choices here; bot-level ones on your computer.
ux.l1.row.taskFolder: For 12 hours in this conversation, in {folder}
ux.l1.row.taskPlace: For 12 hours in this conversation, on {place}
ux.l1.row.taskCommand: For 12 hours in this conversation, for this command
ux.l1.row.taskPayee: For 12 hours in this conversation, to {payee}
ux.l1.row.alwaysFolder: Always, for deleting in {folder} (covers its subfolders)
ux.l1.row.alwaysUnplaced: Always, this exact command here (any engine, same folder and text)
ux.l1.row.alwaysExact: Always, this exact command here (this engine, this folder)
ux.l1.outcome.stopped: {bot} stopped waiting for this. Ask it again.
ux.l1.added.nothingNew: Approved. {bot} already had this, so nothing new was added.
ux.l1.added.takenBack: Taken back. Anything already done stays done.
ux.l1.added.partial: Some of this was not taken back. Still kept: {list}.
ux.l1.added.onComputer: Take this back on your computer, under {bot} › Level.
ux.l1.settings.title: Things you said yes to for good
ux.l1.settings.intro: {bot} does these without asking. Payments are never kept here: paying asks each time, or for 12 hours in one conversation.
ux.l1.settings.empty: Nothing yet. When you choose Always on an approval, it shows up here.
ux.l1.settings.couldNot: Could not take it back. Try again.
ux.l1.settings.task: Allowed for the next 12 hours in open conversations: {n}
ux.l1.settings.clearLabel: Clear what is allowed for the next 12 hours in open conversations
ux.l1.settings.couldNotClear: Could not clear them. Try again.
ux.l1.level.chipHeader: Changes this conversation only. Routines keep their own level. {bot}'s default for new conversations is {level}, under {bot} › Level.
ux.l1.level.askDetail: Asks before each action that needs your yes. Writing in its own folder goes ahead.
ux.l1.level.autoDetail: Asks before paying, emailing someone new, posting in public, or deleting outside its folder.
ux.l1.level.fullDetail: Still asks before paying, emailing someone new, posting in public, deleting outside its folder, or reading your keys and passwords.
ux.l1.level.unlimitedDetail: Runs everything without asking, except reading your keys and passwords and commands Murage recognizes as able to wipe your computer, which ask first.
ux.l1.level.tableHeading: What each level does, for a turn with nothing you said yes to before
ux.l1.level.row.read-given: Read email, calendar and files it was given
ux.l1.level.row.destructive-inside-or-in: A command that looks destructive inside its folder, or may wait for input
ux.l1.level.row.message-known: Email or message someone it has written to before
ux.l1.level.row.someone-new-or-public: Email someone new, or post in public
ux.l1.level.row.delete-outside: Delete outside its own folder, on GitHub or in a database
ux.l1.level.row.contact-bot: Contact another bot (when "Ask me before contacting other bots" is on)
ux.l1.level.row.wipe-command: A command that could wipe this computer
ux.l1.level.stopColumn: Someone new, a public post, a delete outside or a payment
ux.l1.level.other.owner-channel: Your messages from Telegram, Slack or Discord
ux.l1.level.other.other-channel-or-webho: Anyone else's channel message, or a webhook
ux.l1.level.cell.lower-of-ceiling: Runs at the lower of the routine's level and this one
ux.l1.level.cell.asks-unless-routine-gra: Asks, unless allowed for the routine
ux.l1.level.cell.goes-ahead-with-option: Goes ahead only with "Also skip approvals for my messages" on
ux.l1.level.note.never-for-payment: A payment is never allowed for a routine.
ux.l1.level.note.reads-and-own-folder-go: Reads and its own folder still go.
ux.l1.level.underTable: Routines keep their own level and never run above this one. Your messages from Telegram, Slack and Discord ask each step unless you turn that off under Full access. Deny rules and the never-list apply at every level.
ux.l1.level.lockLine: Full access and No limits are set on your computer, where you can see what they change.
